# AI & Deep Learning {#hero-title}

A three-week, hands-on introduction to deep learning and modern AI — from a single
neuron to a working GPT you build yourself. We start with the maths, write
back-propagation by hand, scale up in PyTorch, and finish by building (and critiquing)
a small language model.

::: {.cta}
[Browse the lectures](lectures.qmd){.btn-cta}
[Go to the labs](labs.qmd){.btn-cta .secondary}
[Reading list](readings.qmd){.btn-cta .ghost}
:::
:::

## What you'll be able to do

By the end of the course you will be able to:

1. **Explain** what (deep) neural networks are and how they're trained.
2. **Build** neural networks from scratch in Python, then scale up with PyTorch.
3. **Apply** deep learning to predict, classify, and generate.
4. **Critique** AI systems — their assumptions, failure modes, and social consequences.

::: {.callout-note}
This is a *technical* course: we write code, do calculus, and read papers. The goal is
**understanding** — neural networks are not magic; they rest on fairly simple maths,
built up one careful step at a time.
:::

## The shape of the course

Each day pairs a **3-hour lecture** with a **90-minute lab**. The lectures build the
ideas; the labs make you implement them. The labs deliberately reuse the previous day's
code, so across three weeks you assemble one continuous project that ends in a
working transformer language model.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Week 1]{.week-pill} — Foundations
1. What do we mean by *AI*?
2. Deep models — a primer
3. Computational graphs & the maths of AI
4. Backpropagation
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Week 2]{.week-pill} — Vision & generation
5. Feed-forward networks in PyTorch
6. Classifying images (CNNs)
7. Generating images (VAEs, diffusion)
8. Text-gen 1/4 — embeddings & character models
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
### [Week 3]{.week-pill} — Text & LLMs
9. Text-gen 2/4 — recurrent networks
10. Text-gen 3/4 — attention & transformers
11. Text-gen 4/4 — tokenisation & sampling
12. Ethics, limitations & recap
:::

:::

## The build, day by day

The labs are a single staircase. Each step reuses the last:

> numpy neuron → your own autograd (`Value`) → PyTorch nets → CNN → VAE → character
> bigram → RNN → **transformer (GPT)** → byte-pair encoding + sampling → and, as the
> capstone, a complete GPT written in **pure Python** on the very `Value` class you
> wrote in week 1.

Each lab is a guided notebook with `# TODO` cells for you to fill in and worked solutions
at the end. You run them in Google Colab — nothing to install.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Material goes up as we reach it.** [Lectures](lectures.qmd) and [labs](labs.qmd) for
week 1 are posted now; weeks 2 and 3 follow day by day. The [reading list](readings.qmd)
covers all three weeks already if you want to get ahead.
:::
